why: The second refit failed only the training group (California, Iberia), because its shorter rain residence time, needed to give South Brazil and Japan back their rain, wets winter-rain coasts that are already too wet. r39's winter columns are 1.3-1.85x NCEP's precipitable water in 14 regions, and the winter rain error follows them (r 0.67 in log); e58 (one-sided: the sea's column water saturates at the column temperature where that is colder than the sea) dries East Asia's and East Australia's winters and moves the training group to 0.988 on the second winner, but costs South Brazil, Japan and the British Isles annual rain they already lack. This search lets the residence time, the shelf rule and e58 settle that trade-off together. Land friction on the zonal belts (e57) is net harmful and is left out.
